key_insight: An automated pipeline using open-source LLMs and fine-tuned vision foundation models can help diagnose major cardiac diseases from routine CMR images with strong performance.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce manual labeling burden and support more scalable, standardized CMR interpretation for conditions such as HCM, DCM, ICM, cardiac amyloidosis, and normal controls.
method: Used locally run open-source LLMs to extract diagnostic labels from narrative CMR reports.
Preprocessed cine and late-gadolinium-enhancement CMR data into a multimodal training pipeline.
Fine-tuned three vision foundation models (DINO, VST, UMedPT) in a two-stage approach and combined them with ensemble strategies.
evidence_signal: The model was trained on 988 curated cases and evaluated on an independent test set of 1067 patients, with top AUCs reaching 0.959 for HCM and 0.966 for cardiac amyloidosis.
watch_item: Performance is promising, but real-world deployment still depends on external validation, workflow integration, and careful handling of site-specific report language and imaging variation.
paper_title: Development of an automated, reliable, and clinically meaningful artificial intelligence (AI) tool for diagnosing cardiac disease from conventional cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) images
